Which crops suit the sahel zone?

What grows well in the sahel zone is decided by the length and reliability of the rains. Very short erratic season, roughly 250 to 500mm. Millet, sorghum, cowpea. Drought escape through short duration varieties matters more than yield potential. Plant on established rains, not on the first shower, in every zone. A false start is the most expensive common mistake. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are available and registered in your area.

I want to start beekeeping. What should I know?

This is one of the places where a small holding gains or loses money fastest. Site hives away from paths and livestock, with shade and a nearby water source. Harvest leaving enough honey for the colony to hold through the dearth. Deworm on a schedule appropriate to the season and local advice, since worm pressure rises in the wet season. Brooders start warm and step down week by week. Chick behaviour is the best gauge: huddling under the heat means too cold, spread to the edges panting means too hot, evenly spread means correct. Keep a simple record of what you did and when, because next season that record is worth more than any general advice.

My tomatoes have black sunken patches on the bottom of the fruit. Which insecticide should I buy?

None. An insecticide will not help here, and I would rather save you the money.

Black sunken patches at the blossom end of the fruit are blossom end rot, which is a disorder rather than a pest or a disease. Nothing is eating the fruit. The plant cannot move enough calcium into the developing fruit, and irregular watering is usually the reason, because calcium travels with water.

What actually helps:

1. Water regularly and evenly rather than letting the soil dry out and then soaking it.
2. Mulch to hold soil moisture steady between waterings.
3. Avoid heavy nitrogen while fruit is setting, since fast leafy growth pulls calcium away from the fruit.

Affected fruit will not recover, so remove them. Fruit that sets after you stabilise the watering should be clean. If your soil is genuinely low in calcium, your extension officer can advise on liming, but fix the watering first because that is usually the whole problem.

How do I package produce for market?

This is one of the cheapest places on a smallholding to gain or lose money. Packaging is not decoration. Grading and clean uniform packs get a better price for the same produce and reduce rejection. Rigid crates instead of raffia baskets sharply reduce bruising and rejection on arrival at market. Hermetic bags control storage insects without chemicals, but only if the liner is sealed properly every time. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are available and registered in your area.

My soybean is underperforming. Where do I start?

The levers on soybean are few and worth working in order of cost. Rows about 50 to 75cm apart with plants close within the row, aiming for a dense even stand that shades out weeds. Harvest as soon as pods are dry and rattling. Leaving it standing invites shattering, and shattered grain on the ground is lost. An excellent break crop before maize. The nitrogen it leaves behind cuts the following season's fertiliser bill. Inoculating seed with rhizobium before planting is a small cost that raises nitrogen fixation and yield, especially on land that has not grown soybean before.
I already did that and it did not help. What else?

A problem that returns each season usually means the source was never removed rather than that the treatment failed. Look at what carries it over: infected planting material, crop residues left in the field, a neighbouring plot, or soil fertility that never recovered. An excellent break crop before maize. I have newcastle disease in my poultry. What should I do?

Work through newcastle disease cheapest first. Vaccination on schedule is the control. There is no treatment once the flock breaks. Local backyard flocks benefit most, since they are usually unvaccinated. Sudden high mortality across the flock, twisted necks and nervous signs, greenish droppings, sharp drop in laying. Isolate new or returning birds before mixing, restrict visitor access, and never bring birds back from market into the flock unquarantined.

Look at what carries it over: infected planting material, crop residues left in the field, a neighbouring plot, or soil fertility that never recovered. How do I stop black sigatoka coming back next season?

Preventing black sigatoka is far cheaper than treating it once it is established.

1. Remove and destroy affected leaves, widen spacing for airflow, and keep the stool desuckered. Nutrition matters, since a well fed plant holds more functional leaves.

The most common mistake here is acting late. Start with the cheapest item on this list and watch the crop for two weeks before deciding whether more is needed.

What is the right way to handle cassava after harvest?

This is one of the cheapest places on a smallholding to gain or lose money. Ferment and process within 48 hours of harvest. Fermentation is also what lowers cyanogen levels in garri and fufu. Selling as a group gives access to buyers who will not deal in small lots, and spreads the cost of transport and storage. It is usually the largest single price gain available to a smallholder. Dry grain to roughly 13 percent before storage. Grain that feels dry in the afternoon sun can still be too wet to store safely. Your local extension officer can confirm which varieties and products are available and registered in your area.

What is the right way to deal with tuta absoluta on tomato?

Control of tuta absoluta on tomato works best as a sequence, cheapest first.

1. Exclusion netting over nurseries, pheromone traps for monitoring and mass trapping, removal and destruction of affected material, and rotation away from tomato and related crops.

Cost matters as much as effectiveness on a small holding, so do the cheap things first. Work down this list in order. The early items cost little and prevent most of the damage the later ones try to repair.

Walk me through planting maize on a small plot.

Getting maize established well matters more than anything you do later in the season, because a weak stand cannot be rescued by fertiliser.

1. 75cm between rows and 25cm within rows, one plant per stand, about 53,000 plants per hectare.
2. Split nitrogen: a basal compound fertiliser at planting, then top dress with urea at about 3 to 4 weeks, and again at knee height on poor soils. Place fertiliser in a band beside the plant, not broadcast, to cut losses.

Moisture stress at tasselling and silking causes the largest yield loss of any stage. Start with the cheapest item on this list and watch the crop for two weeks before deciding whether more is needed.

My sweet potato is not doing well. How do I work out the problem?

On sweet potato the usual causes are a short list, so work through them before treating anything.

What to look for:
- Check for sweet potato weevil.
- Check for vine cuttings taken from diseased stock.
- Check for cracking from irregular moisture.

The common problems on sweet potato are sweet potato weevil, vine cuttings taken from diseased stock, cracking from irregular moisture. Match the symptom to the cause before you spend money. The wrong treatment costs cash and loses the window for the right one. Work down this list in order. The early items cost little and prevent most of the damage the later ones try to repair.

What is the right way to start keeping rabbits?

This is one of the places where a small holding gains or loses money fastest. Low capital, fast turnover, and they eat forage rather than competing with the household for grain. Housing must stay dry and well ventilated. Dry season feed is the binding constraint. Conserve crop residues and plan supplementation before the shortage arrives, not during it. Backyard flocks give the best return on very small capital, but only if Newcastle vaccination is kept up. Unvaccinated flocks are periodically wiped out.
